skill.name: claude-reflect
skill.description: Guides Claude Code through a reflection workflow that captures user corrections, reviews queued learnings, and updates memory files with approval.
skill.summary: Capture Claude Code corrections and route approved learnings to memory files.
skill.author: BayramAnnakov

security_audit.summary: The static command, network, and reconnaissance alerts are mostly markdown documentation false positives. The filesystem alerts are confirmed because the skill intentionally reads and writes Claude Code memory, rules, queues, settings, session history, and command files under hidden directories.

remediation.issue: Persistent writes to agent memory files
remediation.suggestion: Show a destination, diff, and scope choice before every write. Keep global memory updates disabled until the user explicitly selects them.

remediation.issue: Session history scanning and long retention
remediation.suggestion: Limit scan ranges by default, exclude sensitive projects, and avoid recommending very long session retention as the default setup.
Create drafts first, require human review, and label generated instructions before writing to command directories.
Prefer Claude Code uninstall or update commands, or provide a guarded cleanup script that verifies exact plugin paths.

semantic_findings.title: Persistent Agent Memory Modification
semantic_findings.description: The skill is designed to place approved corrections into global and project Claude Code memory files. This can persist instructions across future sessions and projects.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Multiple files describe the same memory destinations, including global ~/.claude files and project command directories. The behavior is core to the skill design.

semantic_findings.title: Session History Mining Privacy Risk
semantic_findings.description: The workflow analyzes local Claude Code session history to find corrections and repeated work patterns. Session files may contain sensitive prompts, paths, and project context.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The documentation explicitly describes scanning past sessions and increasing session retention. The privacy concern follows directly from those data sources.

semantic_findings.title: Generated Skill File Persistence
semantic_findings.description: The skill can generate or update command files from observed user behavior. Incorrectly accepted output could create persistent agent workflows or guardrails.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The README and repository guidance describe generated skill files and routing corrections back into skill definitions. Human approval lowers risk but does not remove persistence impact.

content.value_statement: AI assistants lose important corrections between sessions. Claude Reflect queues corrections for review and applies approved learnings to Claude Code memory files.
actual_capabilities: Reminds users to run reflection after corrections or completed work.
Documents a review flow for queued learning items.
Routes approved learnings to global, project, local, and rule files.
Supports historical session review for missed corrections.
Describes skill candidate discovery from repeated workflows.
Explains export paths for Claude Code and AGENTS.md memory.
limitations: This snapshot mainly contains documentation and skill context files.
Operational hooks and scripts are referenced but not included in this package.
The workflow reads or writes local Claude Code memory and session files.
Detection quality depends on user review and clear correction wording.

use_cases.title: Preserve Project Preferences
use_cases.description: A developer can convert repeated corrections into reviewed project memory for future Claude Code sessions.

use_cases.title: Standardize Team Guardrails
use_cases.description: A team lead can review recurring workflow mistakes and turn approved guidance into shared agent rules.

use_cases.title: Find Reusable Workflows
use_cases.description: A power user can scan prior sessions for repeated tasks that may become reusable commands.

prompt_templates.title: Review Pending Learnings
prompt_templates.prompt: Show my pending learnings and help me decide which ones should be applied to memory.

prompt_templates.title: Apply Project Guidance
prompt_templates.scenario: Store a correction for one repository
prompt_templates.prompt: Reflect on this correction and suggest a project-level learning with a short explanation.

prompt_templates.title: Scan Past Sessions
prompt_templates.prompt: Review recent sessions for repeated corrections and summarize the strongest memory candidates.

prompt_templates.title: Discover Skill Candidates
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze repeated workflows across my sessions and propose reusable command ideas with evidence and review notes.

output_examples.input: The user corrects Claude to always run tests before deployment.
output_examples.output: A reviewed learning is proposed for the project: run the test suite before any deployment step.

output_examples.input: The user asks to review recent sessions for repeated productivity workflows.
output_examples.output: The skill summarizes recurring workflow candidates and asks which drafts should be created.

output_examples.input: The user wants to see pending learning items without applying them.
output_examples.output: The skill lists queued items, confidence notes, and suggested destinations for review.

best_practices: Review every learning before writing it to global memory.
Keep project-specific conventions in project files, not global files.
Use dry-run or preview flows before applying large memory changes.
anti_patterns: Do not approve vague corrections that lack future value.
Do not store secrets, tokens, or private project details in memory.
Do not scan all historical sessions without checking privacy impact.

faq.question: What does Claude Reflect do?
faq.answer: It helps review user corrections and turn approved items into persistent Claude Code memory.

faq.question: Does it update files automatically?
faq.answer: The documented workflow requires human review before applying queued learnings.

faq.question: Which tools does it support?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Can it scan old sessions?
faq.answer: Yes. The documentation describes session history review for missed corrections and workflow patterns.

faq.question: What should users review carefully?
faq.answer: Users should check global memory writes, generated command files, and any session history scan.

faq.question: Is this package implementation complete?
faq.answer: This reviewed snapshot mainly includes documentation and skill context. Referenced hooks and scripts are not included here.
